question: Where should the new analyzers be built first?

options.A: Inside the live app as add-on modules behind a tab layer
options.B: In a separate isolated preview app on its own address, leaving the live app untouched
options.C: Isolated preview first, then port proven modules into the live app

question: How should each dashboard's analyzer tabs be organised?

options.A: 3-4 tabs grouped from existing cards, every existing card mapped to a tab, merged or hidden
options.B: Exactly 4 task-focused tabs per dashboard, each with inputs, 3 KPIs, one main chart and expandable calculation, assumptions and evidence
options.C: Codex's 4 task-focused tab layout, plus Claude's card map so no existing card is lost

question: How should price year selection work?

options.A: Price basis inherited from the scope bar; one year per scenario
options.B: An explicit analysis-basis drawer: historical or forecast mode, one or many years, duration/equal/custom weighting, strict coverage, audit of included years
options.C: Codex's analysis-basis drawer, plus Claude's one-bus-one-price and no-mixed-basis rules

question: Which connection-capacity value should the Grid analyzer treat as governing?

options.A: The element-study limit (lowest facility transfer), with the substation envelope shown as an unreconciled vendor alternative
options.B: Published envelope minus requested MW per case, with study coverage shown
options.C: Show both by case; the governing value is the element-study limit, flagged when the two disagree

question: Should nearby queued projects be subtracted from connection headroom?

options.A: Yes, subtract not-in-model queued MW weighted by survival and distribution-factor ratio
options.B: Never subtract geographically nearby queue MW; show it as context only unless study participation is documented
options.C: Do not subtract by default; offer the weighted subtraction as a labelled what-if scenario

question: How should the upgrade cost allocator work?

options.A: Step function from study facility transfers and costs, share by distribution-factor proportional impact, labelled proxy
options.B: User-editable scope rows (direct, network, affected-system), named allocation scenario, known subtotal plus unpriced scope, no interpolation
options.C: Codex's editable scope and subtotal model, pre-filled from study facility costs, with the distribution-factor share offered as one named scenario

question: How should battery storage value be calculated?

options.A: Daily top-n minus bottom-n price spread with round-trip efficiency, labelled perfect-foresight ceiling
options.B: Chronological state-of-charge dispatch with power, energy, efficiency and POI limits, labelled perfect-foresight benchmark
options.C: Chronological dispatch as the main result, with the spread ceiling shown only as a quick screening benchmark

question: How should hybrid solar-plus-storage be valued?

options.A: Clipping recapture replaces grid charging; battery value counted once
options.B: One shared chronological energy balance with shared inverter and POI limits, no overlapping revenues
options.C: Codex's shared energy balance, with Claude's no-double-count and charging-deliverability checks as tests

question: How should project finance be handled?

options.A: LCOE/NPV/IRR only when the user enters O&M, financing and tax inputs; otherwise not shown
options.B: Chronological annual cash flows from a named forecast path, NPV/IRR where defined, incomplete valuation when inputs are missing
options.C: Codex's chronological cash flows, with Claude's rule that no tax-credit or financing default is ever assumed

question: How should the Decision dashboard compare options?

options.A: Weighted scorecard on ISO-wide percentiles plus gate verdicts where unknown is never a pass
options.B: Side-by-side raw metrics and requirements, optional preference score after compatibility checks, readiness actions and an immutable decision record
options.C: Codex's side-by-side comparison and decision record, with Claude's gate verdicts and tie band

question: How should missing or unstudied data be displayed?

options.A: Not held / unknown with the reason; never zero; true zeros printed in units
options.B: Unknown stays unknown; material omissions produce incomplete results or known subtotals
options.C: Both: Claude's not-held/true-zero display rules plus Codex's incomplete-result and known-subtotal behaviour

question: Which visual design should the analyzers use?

options.A: The existing dark-first app frame and tokens
options.B: A quieter light design: white surfaces, pale neutral background, dark slate text, one teal action colour, status colours always labelled
options.C: Codex's quiet light design with a dark theme option using the same tokens

question: Which dashboards should be implemented first?

options.A: By calculator priority: Market screening and Grid headroom first
options.B: Prices, then Grid, then Economics, because price years feed revenue and connection limits
options.C: Prices, Grid and Economics first (connected flow), then Market, Queue, Land and Decision

question: How should interconnection rules (deposits, clocks, allocation) be encoded?

options.A: Federal Order 2023 pro forma constants, labelled pro forma, ISO-specific amounts marked not held
options.B: A regional process profile per provider with effective rule version and source references; no single national formula
options.C: Codex's regional process profiles, seeded with the Order 2023 pro forma as the first labelled profile
